title: Proteogenomic re-identification policy (variant-peptide default-deny)
context: Mass-spec proteomics data carries a proteogenomic re-identification risk: variant (single-amino-acid-variant / SAV) peptides detected in open-access DDA data can encode germline SNP information functionally equivalent to a genetic identifier, enabling individual re-identification even from nominally de-identified public datasets. Without a published default-deny policy and a per-dataset reviewer-clearance process, this risk can be violated inadvertently. The policy must be in place before any dataset is cleared for analysis, and it must be blocked by the allow-list gate.
objective: Publish the project's proteogenomic re-identification policy establishing a default-deny stance for variant/SAV peptide outputs and the conditions under which the License+Compliance reviewer may clear a specific dataset and use for variant search.
acceptanceCriteria: The policy states that variant/proteogenomic identity output (variant/SAV peptides, per-individual genotype-equivalent calls) is default-denied for all datasets unless the License+Compliance reviewer explicitly clears the specific dataset and use case in writing.

The conditions required for reviewer clearance are defined: e.g., the source license explicitly permits re-id-risk outputs, the dataset is provably cell-line or fully synthetic, or an IRB authorization exists — with no default-allow path.
The policy specifies that sample-level outputs are kept aggregate where individual-level results add re-identification risk without research need.
The policy is referenced in the allow-list gate (allowlist-002) as a required determination field (reidDetermination) before any dataset is approved.
The policy document is licensed CC-BY-4.0 and committed to the project repo.
